Rumors of the foldable iPhone Ultra are just weeks away from launch. As we mentioned earlier, market anticipation for this device continues to grow.

A new Bloomberg report today compiles what Apple employees who have tried the iPhone Ultra liked about it.

iPhone Ultra launch nears: real hands-on impressions

In the latest issue of his Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman takes an in-depth look at this foldable iPhone. He specifically mentions having spoken with "several" people who have tried the device. These people said they particularly liked the following:

  • How well the device fits in a pocket. The cover display is reportedly 5.5 inches.
  • The durability of the hinge.
  • The new "iPad-like app layout" that makes full use of the inner display, which is reportedly around 7.8 inches and wider in landscape than portrait orientation.
  • How well it performs as a "camera viewfinder."

Multiple reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will be priced above two thousand US dollars. It's expected to feature main and ultra-wide cameras, but no telephoto lens. It will reportedly use Touch ID instead of Face ID for biometrics.

9to5Mac's take

I'm very excited about the iPhone Ultra, and the details Gurman has revealed make me even more convinced it's the right device for me.

I was initially somewhat hesitant about the design of a foldable iPhone, but as I've learned more about its size and advantages, I've changed my mind.

The positive reception of Samsung's latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 provides a useful real-world reference, as its form factor is very similar to that of the iPhone Ultra.

Of course, compared to the iPhone 18 Pro there will inevitably be some shortcomings. I'm currently using the iPhone Air, so I've already grown accustomed to life without a telephoto lens, and going back to Touch ID doesn't feel like much of a sacrifice.

What are your thoughts on the iPhone Ultra rumors? Will you be buying one this fall? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
